subject: Literature
title: Allen Ginsberg's Howl and the Beat Generation
description: A quick win: understand Allen Ginsberg's Howl and the Beat Generation.

hook.text: US Customs seized copies of Allen Ginsberg's poem Howl at the San Francisco docks and charged the publisher.

buildup.text: Howl celebrated drug use, homosexuality, and spiritual ecstasy in language that shocked 1950s America.

discovery.text: Publisher Lawrence Ferlinghetti deliberately provoked the trial to test and expand free speech protections.

twist.text: The judge ruled Howl had 'redeeming social importance,' a legal standard that protected controversial art for decades.

climax.text: The trial made Ginsberg famous and turned the Beat Generation from an underground movement into a cultural force.

punchline.text: The government tried to silence a poem and made it immortal.

quiz.question: Why did Ferlinghetti deliberately publish Howl despite the risk?
options: He did not know it would be controversial
He wanted to provoke a trial to test and expand free speech protections
He was paid a large sum to publish it
